cita: Sharma (2026). Shodh-Memory: A Cognitive Memory System for Edge-Native AI Agents.
problema: Cloud-dependent agent memory (e.g. Mem0) imposes latency/connectivity constraints incompatible with edge deployment, and existing systems treat associations as static and give all memories uniform importance regardless of type, age or access pattern.
mecanismo: Three-tier architecture (working/session/long-term, Cowan's model) with importance/age tier-promotion thresholds; piecewise exponential-to-power-law decay with a consolidation crossover at tc=3 days; dual Hebbian plasticity (asymmetric importance updates on feedback + synaptic edge strengthening with tier-dependent learning rates) plus multi-scale LTP (Burst/Weekly/Full); retrieval fuses BM25+vector+graph spreading activation with density-dependent fusion weights.
evaluacion: Single-binary Rust systems evaluation on one commodity-hardware machine: Criterion.rs microbenchmarks of core operations, knowledge-graph operation latency, and end-to-end API latency/scaling; NO standardized retrieval-quality benchmark (e.g. LOCOMO) is run against ground-truth QA -- the paper explicitly defers that to future work, reporting only synthetic Precision@k/Recall@k/MRR scenarios.
numeros_clave: Sub-20ms end-to-end store/recall with 100% offline capability; core in-memory ops 9ns-565us (Table3, e.g. working-memory activation 9.35ns, concurrent 10-thread reads 565us); synthetic (non-benchmark) scenarios show 20-40% Recall@5 gain and 30% MRR gain for graph-augmented vs vector-only retrieval; cites Mem0's reported cloud P95 latency of 200-500ms as context (Sec2.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A single-binary, 100%-offline edge deployment reaching sub-20ms operations (Sec5.5) is a concrete pattern MF could mine for zero-network-latency, local-first memory retrieval design.
The idle-period consolidation pipeline that clusters aged episodic memories by Jaccard similarity into semantic facts with provenance links (Sec3.5) is a reusable gotcha->fact promotion mechanism.

Asymmetric importance plasticity (additive boost vs multiplicative decay on positive/negative feedback, Sec3.3.1) tracks memory trustworthiness over time, relevant context though not validated against a real QA benchmark.

notes: Numbers from Table3/4 (Criterion.rs benchmarks) and Sec5.1/6.3; RECONSIDERAR -- retrieval-quality claims (the RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO facet) rest only on synthetic scenarios, not a standard benchmark like LOCOMO, which the paper itself lists as future work (Sec2.3, Sec6.3).

cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory V3: Information-Geometric Foundations for Zero-LLM Enterprise Agent Memory.
problema: Current memory systems retrieve via cosine similarity, decay via heuristic exponential schedules, and provide no formal mechanism to detect contradictions across contexts -- an 'engineering monoculture' whose optimality, convergence and correctness are mathematically unexamined, especially under EU AI Act data-sovereignty constraints that favor zero-cloud operation.
mecanismo: Three mathematical layers integrated into a four-channel retrieval architecture: (1) Fisher-information-weighted retrieval replacing cosine similarity with a per-dimension-variance-weighted Fisher-Rao distance (Theorem 6.1, Theta(d) time); (2) memory lifecycle modeled as Riemannian Langevin dynamics with a proven-unique stationary retention distribution (Fokker-Planck, Theorem 6.3); (3) the memory store modeled as a cellular sheaf where non-trivial first cohomology H^1 flags irreconcilable cross-context contradictions (Sec5.4).
evaluacion: LoCoMo benchmark, six conversations (n=832 questions) scored by LLM-as-Judge, comparing the three-math-layer system to an ablated 'engineering baseline'; a separate small cloud-augmented test on a single conversation (n=81); component ablation table isolating each layer's contribution.
numeros_clave: +12.7pp average accuracy improvement over the engineering baseline across six LoCoMo conversations, up to +19.9pp on the hardest one (Table5); zero-LLM/zero-cloud configuration reaches ~75% retrieval accuracy; a single-conversation cloud-augmented test (n=81) reaches 87.7%; ablation: removing cross-encoder reranking alone costs -30.7pp, the single largest component (Table4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Sheaf-cohomology contradiction detection (H^1(F)!=0 flags irreconcilable local-to-global claims, Sec5.4) is a formal, testable mechanism for MF's staleness/poisoning detection beyond heuristic similarity checks.

The sheaf assigns local memory claims to context-vertices with restriction maps enforcing cross-seam compatibility (Sec2.6), directly analogous to MF's multi-store seam problem, though demonstrated only at toy scale (six conversations).

Ablation (Table4/5) measures that principled retrieval math (Fisher metric + reranking) beats a plain-cosine engineering baseline by double-digit points, supporting a measured-retrieval stance, though on a very small sample (n=832/n=81) from a single independent researcher.

notes: Numbers from Table4/5 (LoCoMo ablation, Sec7); RECONSIDERAR -- a single independent-researcher arXiv preprint making grandiose proven-theorem claims (Fisher metric, sheaf cohomology, Langevin dynamics) validated on only six conversations plus one n=81 cloud test, no peer review.

cita: Fofadiya & Tiwari (2026). Multi-Layered Memory Architectures for LLM Agents: An Experimental Evaluation of Long-Term Context Retention.
problema: Long-horizon dialogue systems suffer semantic drift and unstable memory retention across extended sessions because naive concatenation of dialogue history causes quadratic context growth and memory interference, and prior approaches trade efficiency against retention stability rather than achieving both.
mecanismo: Decomposes dialogue history into working/episodic/semantic memory layers (Eq.2): a bounded-window working memory (Eq.4), an exponential-decay recursively-blended episodic summary (Eq.5), and an entity-event-graph semantic abstraction (Eq.6); softmax adaptive layer-gating weights retrieval across the three layers (Eq.7-8); a retention-regularization loss penalizes abrupt shifts in semantic-memory embeddings across sessions (Eq.9), jointly optimized with the generation objective (Eq.10).
evaluacion: Evaluated on three benchmarks named LOCOMO, LOCCO and LoCoMo, reporting Success Rate/F1/BLEU/six-period retention/context-usage against numbers drawn from many unrelated prior papers (including task-planning benchmarks like Blocksworld/Gripper/Tyreworld); per-component ablation removing the semantic layer, episodic consolidation, retention loss, and adaptive gating.
numeros_clave: On 'LOCOMO': SR 46.85 vs a cited 42.00 baseline (Table2); on 'LoCoMo': overall F1=0.618 (multi-hop F1=0.594) vs a cited prior 0.583; on 'LOCCO': six-period retention 56.90% vs 48.25%, false-memory rate 5.1% vs 6.8%, context usage 58.40% vs 64.98% (Table IV); ablation (Table V): removing the semantic layer drops F1 0.618->0.591 and retention 56.90%->50.84%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The recursive alpha-blended episodic-to-semantic consolidation (Eq.5-6) is a candidate promotion mechanism, though the paper's cross-paper number reuse (see notes) makes the ablation deltas (Table V) hard to trust at face value.
The retention-regularization loss (Eq.9) explicitly penalizes semantic-memory drift across sessions, conceptually relevant to MF's anti-staleness concern.
Reports lower context usage (58.40% vs 64.98%, Table IV) alongside better F1, matching MF's cost-quality tradeoff framing, but weighted lightly given the baseline-comparison issue noted below.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- Table II/III attribute an SR of 42.00 to Hu et al. under a 'LOCOMO' column, yet the paper's own Literature Review (Sec II) describes that number as coming from Blocksworld/Gripper/Tyreworld/Barman/Jericho task-planning benchmarks, not LOCOMO; the paper also defines three near-identically-named benchmarks (LOCOMO/LOCCO/LoCoMo) and compares against numbers cited from many unrelated papers as if directly comparable -- evidentiary rigor is doubtful.

cita: Liu et al. (2026). Omni-SimpleMem: Autoresearch-Guided Discovery of Lifelong Multimodal Agent Memory.
problema: Building effective lifelong multimodal agent memory requires jointly tuning architecture, retrieval strategy, prompt engineering and data pipelines -- a design space too large and interconnected for manual research or traditional AutoML (which cannot do code comprehension, bug diagnosis, or cross-component architectural redesign) to explore effectively.
mecanismo: A 23-stage autonomous LLM research pipeline (AutoResearchClaw) iteratively hypothesizes, implements, and evaluates changes to a text-only starting codebase (SimpleMem), converging on: selective ingestion (novelty-filtered multimodal inputs encapsulated as Multimodal Atomic Units that split hot-storage metadata/embeddings from lazily-loaded cold raw content); progressive pyramid retrieval (hybrid dense+BM25 set-union merge, then 3-stage summary->detail->raw-content expansion under a token budget); and a knowledge-graph layer for multi-hop entity reasoning with entity resolution and distance-decayed relevance.
evaluacion: LoCoMo and Mem-Gallery (1,711 QA pairs over 240 multimodal dialogues) across five LLM backbones vs six baselines (MemVerse, Mem0, Claude-Mem, A-MEM, MemGPT, SimpleMem); ablation removing pyramid expansion, BM25 hybrid search, and other components; the ~50-experiment autonomous optimization trajectory itself is logged and analyzed (~72h wall-clock).
numeros_clave: LoCoMo F1 improved +411% from the naive baseline (0.117->0.598) and Mem-Gallery F1 +214% (0.254->0.797); on GPT-4o, overall LoCoMo F1=0.598 vs best baseline SimpleMem 0.432 (Table1); ablation (Sec4.4.1): removing pyramid expansion costs -17% F1, removing BM25 hybrid search -14% (mean over 4 backbones); a single one-line bug fix (missing response_format param) alone drove +175% of the LoCoMo improvement (Sec4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The token-budget-gated pyramid retrieval (summaries->details->raw content, Sec3.2.2) is a concrete progressive-disclosure pattern MF could adopt for graduated index-to-docs expansion under a fixed cost budget.
Multimodal Atomic Units splitting compact searchable hot-storage metadata from lazily-loaded cold raw content (Sec3.2.1) directly parallels MF's derived-index-as-cache-over-docs-as-truth split.

The autonomous-research-pipeline itself (an LLM agent diagnosing and fixing its own memory system's bugs, +175% from one bug fix, Sec4.2) is tangential context on automated engineering rather than a claim about MF's write-trigger design.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (per-backbone F1) and Sec4.2/4.4.1 (optimization trajectory + ablation); note the single largest gain (+175% of the LoCoMo improvement) came from fixing a pipeline bug, not a novel memory mechanism -- weight the architectural claims (MAUs, pyramid) below the bug-fix contribution.

cita: Guo et al. (2026). MemFactory: Unified Inference & Training Framework for Agent Memory.
problema: Memory-RL research (using reinforcement learning to optimize agent memory extraction/update/retrieval policies) is fragmented across siloed, task-specific implementations, with no unified infrastructure comparable to LLaMA-Factory for standard fine-tuning, raising the engineering barrier to reproduce or combine strategies like Memory-R1, MemAgent, and RMM.
mecanismo: A four-layer modular framework (Module/Agent/Environment/Trainer) that decomposes the memory lifecycle into atomic plug-and-play modules (Extractor, Updater with ADD/DEL/UPDATE/NONE operations, Retriever, Agent-Module for end-to-end recurrent policies), assembled by an Agent Layer into rollout trajectories, scored by an Environment Layer's multi-dimensional reward manager (format + LLM-as-judge rewards), and fine-tuned by a native Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) Trainer that eliminates the PPO value-network memory overhead via intra-group reward normalization (Eq.1).
evaluacion: Empirical validation reproducing MemAgent-style recurrent memory policies on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B-Instruct, trained via the framework's built-in GRPO pipeline on a single A800 GPU, evaluated on two main-task sets (eval_50/eval_100) and one out-of-distribution set (eval_fwe_16384), scores averaged over 4 trials (avg@4); no ablation of the framework's own components is reported, only base-vs-RL-trained comparison.
numeros_clave: Qwen3-1.7B average score improves 0.3118->0.3581 (+14.8% relative) after MemFactory's GRPO training (Table2); Qwen3-4B-Instruct improves +7.3% relative overall, including gains on the OOD set (eval_fwe_16384: 0.0195->0.0332 for the 1.7B model).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ADD/DEL/UPDATE/NONE four-operation memory-update taxonomy trained via RL for exact-match-optimality (Sec3.1.2) is a reusable pattern MF could weigh for learning rather than hand-designing its gotcha-consolidation policy.
The DEL operation removes obsolete/contradicted facts (Sec3.1.2), touching staleness handling, but MemFactory's own contribution is infrastructure, not a fidelity mechanism per se.

GRPO's elimination of the PPO value-network (halving training-memory footprint, Sec2.3) confirms MF's principle that structural changes, not brute-force scaling, are the real cost lever, here applied to memory-policy training.

notes: Numbers from Table2 (avg@4, Sec4.2); this is primarily an infrastructure/tooling paper (a framework, not a novel memory mechanism), validated on only one reproduced baseline (MemAgent) with modest single-GPU experiments and no internal ablation.

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). GBQA: A Game Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs as Quality Assurance Engineers.
problema: LLM agents struggle to autonomously discover software bugs in dynamic interactive environments -- unlike code generation/repair the objective is ill-defined -- and no existing benchmark provides human-verified ground-truth bugs in reproducible interactive game environments to measure this capability.
mecanismo: The baseline QA agent's hierarchical memory module: in-session working memory keeps a sliding window of recent steps in full detail while older steps are abstraction-oriented-summarized (preserving causal state changes like 'after picking up item X, event Y becomes available', not raw logs); cross-session memory persists a structured distillation (explored regions, confirmed bugs, unresolved hypotheses, priority testing targets) injected into the next session's initial context so testing strategy accumulates across game restarts.
evaluacion: 30 human-verified game environments with 124 bugs (3 difficulty levels) built by a multi-agent generator; a ReAct-based baseline agent evaluated across many frontier LLMs (instruct + thinking) under 2 modes (Player Exploring / Quality Assurance) and 4 step budgets (50/100/200/500), scored by Recall via critic-agent matching against ground truth, validated by human inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's alpha) and Pearson correlation with human ratings.
numeros_clave: Best model (Claude-4.6-Opus-Thinking, QA mode, 500 steps) recalls only 48.39% of 124 ground-truth bugs (Table1); annotation reliability Krippendorff's alpha=0.901 overall (Table2); critic-agent-vs-human agreement Pearson rho up to 0.903 (p<0.0001, Table3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Cross-session memory distilling 'explored regions, confirmed bugs, unresolved hypotheses, priority testing targets' (Sec4.2) into the next session's initial context is a concrete plan-state-as-memory pattern directly matching MF's PLAN-ESTADO need.

In-session vs cross-session memory are two separate stores for two different facts (recent trajectory vs distilled strategy) rather than one source per fact -- tangential context on the seams question.

The step-level reflection/verification mechanism deciding when an anomaly is confident enough to escalate into a formal bug report (Sec4.1) is a discretionary-write-trigger analog, though for bug-reporting rather than memory-writing per se.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- the paper's core contribution is a bug-discovery benchmark for QA agents (ICLR 2026 workshop), not agent-memory research; the hierarchical memory module is only a component of the baseline agent (Sec4.2), not the paper's object of study.
